thread:
alex: quick sanity check please — adding a KMS grant for the vectorizer-worker IRSA role. hoping to avoid granting overly broad principals.
alex: PR: https://gh.redwood/infraproj/terraform/1234 (main change is the aws_kms_grant and a tiny policy tweak)
alex: terraform snippet:
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "vectorizer_irsa" {
  name            = "vectorizer-irsa-grant"
  key_id          = aws_kms_key.app_key.key_id
  grantee_principal = arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/eksctl-vectorizer-NodeInstanceRole-ABCD1234
  operations      = ["Decrypt", "Encrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
  constraints {
    encryption_context_subset = {
      "service" = "vectorizer"
    }
  }
  depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa_trust]
}
```
maria: couple quick things — 1) that grantee_principal looks like the node instance role, not the IRSA role. For IRSA you need the IAM role ARN created by the service account mapping, not the EC2 node role.
alex: ah good catch. the role name comes from the helm values in the vectorizer chart (we generate the role in tf via eks IRSA module). I pasted the wrong ARN here, my bad.
sasha: also watch out for rotation: KMS grants don't automatically update when a role arn changes; we should either reference the role resource directly (aws_iam_role.vectorizer_irsa.arn) or use a key policy that allows the role via aws:PrincipalArn condition. Prefer referencing the role resource.
jon: +1 on referencing the role resource. Also for multi-account we historically add a condition on aws:SourceAccount and kms:EncryptionContext to limit misuse. Something like:
```hcl
condition = {
  test     = "StringEquals"
  variable = "aws:SourceAccount"
  values   = [var.account_id]
}
```
jon: and add encryption_context_subset to only allow when encryption context has "app=vectorizer" so bots can't reuse the grant for other workloads.
alex: thanks. i'm trying to keep this grant usable by pods in the vectorizer namespace only. Do we also need kms:ViaService or anything for IRSA? I remember some gotchas with EKS and STS.
maria: For IRSA the principal is the IAM role that pods assume (sts:AssumeRole). You don't need kms:ViaService. But be careful with session names — we sometimes see long session names that trigger key policy conditions if we match by session tag. Don't rely on session name pattern.
sasha: Another practical point: helm timing + annotation order. If the SA annotation that maps to the IAM role is applied after the pod rollout, the pod won't be able to get creds immediately and will error with AccessDenied on KMS. We put a pre-hook job to wait for annotation propagation in the chart; consider adding that.
alex: good call. i'll add a helm hook that checks `kubectl get sa -n vectorizer vectorizer-worker -o yaml` for the annotation before proceeding.
infra-ci: terraform plan completed in 3m — noted differences in aws_kms_grant referencing. Run `apply` only after role ARN is wired into tf outputs.
deploy-bot: FYI i rolled a staging upgrade earlier and saw one pod fail with DecryptAccessDenied for about 30s during rollout; it recovered when the IRSA role annotation reconciled. :eyes:
jon: that lines up — short window of errors is expected if rollout ordering isn't strict. If SLA matters, we should implement canary pods that use a fallback key or fallback model until grant availability converges.
alex: ok i'll: 1) fix the grantee_principal to use the TF role resource arn, 2) add aws:SourceAccount condition and encryption_context_subset with app=vectorizer, 3) add a helm pre-hook to wait for SA annotation, and 4) run plan & staging apply then watch logs for Decrypt errors.
maria: LGTM for that plan. ping me when PR is updated and i'll review.
alex: thanks all, updating now — will ping when ready. :pray:
